title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 158
paragraphs: When these came to Branchidai, Aristodicos stood forth from the rest and consulted the Oracle, asking as follows: “Lord, there came to us a suppliant for protection, Pactyas the Lydian, fleeing a violent death at the hands of the Persians. They demand him from us, bidding the men of Kyme give him up. But we, though we fear the power of the Persians, have not yet ventured up to this time to deliver to them the suppliant, until your counsel shall be clearly manifested to us, telling which of the two things we ought to do.” He thus inquired, but the god again declared to them the same answer, bidding them deliver up Pactyas to the Persians. Upon this, Aristodicos with deliberate purpose did as follows: he went all round the temple, destroying the nests of sparrows and of all the other kinds of birds which had been hatched on the temple. While he was doing this, it is said that a voice came from the inner shrine directed to Aristodicos, speaking thus: “Most impious of men, why do you dare to do this? Do you carry off by force from my temple the suppliants for my protection?” And Aristodicos, not at all at a loss, replied: “Lord, do you thus come to the assistance of your suppliants, and yet bid the men of Kyme deliver up theirs?” The god answered him again thus: “Yes, I bid you do so, that you may perish the more quickly for your impiety, so that you may not at any future time come to the Oracle to ask about the delivering up of suppliants.”
